thread.title: Lacking Innovation, Can Apple Ever Be A Good Investment Again? (Podcast) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Quoth the Raven
title: Lacking Innovation, Can Apple Ever Be A Good Investment Again? (Podcast) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Given all of the news headlines about Apple ( AAPL ) recently, including my recent interview with Bill Fleckenstein from October , where he predicted Apple's stock slaughter, I thought back to my own history with the company: not only as a product user for nearly 30 years, but also as a one-time employee.
AAPL data by YCharts
As an investment, it’s starting to become clear that Apple has run out of room with its last big innovation, the iPhone. It’s finally starting to appear as though the market is super-saturated and the once ripe piece of low hanging fruit that Steve Jobs passed over to Tim Cook doesn’t appear to have any more meat on the bone.
For Apple to move forward from here, the company undoubtedly needs to innovate once again, as it has arguably gobbled up a significant portion of its total addressable market so far. It needs to make new in-roads into new segments, where it can break into new markets, not only for new customers, but to get existing customers to purchase new products.
Upon this realization, I thought back to my own time at Apple as an employee. Even in the early 2000s, before Steve Jobs died, I personally started to feel a little bit of a culture change at the company. I didn’t know what it was then, but now it’s clear that this was the company changing from the magical beginnings of a turnaround story to a full-fledged corporate behemoth.
For investors, I thought it would be timely and relevant to offer up a high level view of some of the clues that I noticed as an employee and to give my take as to what I believe it is going to take for Apple to be a successful investment again. The company will likely always be a great cash generating entity for a while to come, but with the market cap that once approached $1 trillion and the company succumbing to the law of large numbers, what does the company need to do for it to be a good investment here? I discussed the latest on my podcast.
